findings.title: Retrieval uses only similarity ranking on a shared index, without tenant-based filtering
findings.rationale: The documentation states that all workspaces share a single retrieval index and that "relevance alone" selects which passages are returned. Because resolved support tickets from all workspaces are stored in this index and no workspace/authorization filter is applied at retrieval time, a user's query can retrieve support-history passages originating from other workspaces. This is an inferred weakness from the described design and violates the requirement that retrieval be filtered by the requester's authorization.
findings.evidence_quote: "**Retrieval index** — a managed vector database holding embeddings of the help-center articles and of resolved support tickets. All workspaces are served from one shared index; a query returns the top eight passages ranked by embedding similarity, and relevance alone selects the passages that reach the prompt." (architecture-overview.md)

findings.title: Tenant-aware authorization is not enforced for retrieval over shared support-history corpus
findings.rationale: Workspace-scoped tokens identify the caller's workspace at the API layer, but the retrieval layer is documented to use a shared index for all workspaces and to select passages solely by embedding similarity. This implies that authorization context (the caller’s workspace) is not enforced when accessing stored support-ticket content, so tenant-aware authorization is not applied to this data access path.

findings.title: Embeddings of support tickets from all workspaces are co-mingled without effective tenant separation
findings.rationale: The ingestion pipeline embeds resolved support tickets into a single managed vector database that serves all workspaces, and retrieval over this index is based only on embedding similarity. This design co-mingles stored artifacts (ticket embeddings) from all tenants and does not maintain effective tenant-level separation, especially since retrieval is not constrained by workspace. This is inferred from the explicit description of the shared index and selection mechanism.
findings.evidence_quote:
"**Ingestion pipeline** — the only writer to the retrieval index. It runs nightly, reads two named sources — the published help-center repository and the support platform's resolved tickets export — chunks and embeds them, and records the source and timestamp on every indexed item." (architecture-overview.md)
